record.original_question: Let G = G1*_H G2 be a free pro-p product of coherent pro-p groups with polycyclic amalgamation. Is G coherent? For abstract groups this is known to be true. A group is said to be coherent if each of its finitely generated subgroups is finitely presented, and in the question coherency is used in the pro-p sense.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A pro-p group G is called coherent (in the pro-p sense) if every finitely generated closed subgroup of G is finitely presented as a pro-p group. A pro-p group is polycyclic if it admits a finite subnormal series with procyclic factors. Given pro-p groups G1, G2 and a common closed subgroup H, the free pro-p product with amalgamation G1 *_H G2 is the pushout of G1 and G2 over H in the category of pro-p groups.

Suppose G1 and G2 are coherent pro-p groups, H is a polycyclic pro-p group embedded as a closed subgroup of both G1 and G2, and let G = G1 *_H G2 be the corresponding free pro-p product with polycyclic amalgamation. Is G necessarily coherent in the pro-p sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as a new entry in the 2026 (20th issue) Kourovka Notebook collection of open problems in group theory. No published resolution was found in the search; related results in the abstract group setting are known, but the pro-p analogue with polycyclic amalgamation does not appear to have been settled.

status_evidence.snippet: Contains new problems in group theory including questions about coherence of free pro-p products with polycyclic amalgamation.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the Kourovka Notebook collection.
